report.source_text: At a one-month follow up assessment, OD was painful, had a fully detached retina, anterior segment neovascularization, and an intraocular pressure of 38 mmHg (Figure 1F). The patient only agreed to topical cycloplegic treatment, with mild symptom improvement.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 20-year-old male with a history of right tibial osteosarcoma (diagnosed at age 17, treated with supracondylar amputation) and recent metastatic disease to brain and lungs presented to ophthalmology with decreased vision in the right eye (OD) of 2 weeks' duration. Clinical examination revealed hand movements vision OD with a large, posterior pole, pink, nodular subretinal mass and associated subretinal fluid. B-scan ultrasonography confirmed a subretinal, heterogeneous mass with medium/high reflectivity, areas of necrosis-related decreased reflectivity, and height-to-base ratio of 1-1.2. CT imaging demonstrated a heterogeneous, well-defined uveal mass with hyperdensity, areas of decreased density, significant intraocular involvement, and contrast enhancement. MRI confirmed a well-defined, irregular choroidal mass with T1-isointense and T2-hypointense signal characteristics. At one-month follow-up, the eye had progressed to pain, complete retinal detachment, anterior segment neovascularization, and elevated intraocular pressure (38 mmHg), with the patient receiving only topical cycloplegic treatment with mild symptom improvement.
